messages:
JLee (customer): hey team — we're getting a 400 from the embeddings endpoint when we batch two texts together. works fine single, fails for batch.

Maria (Support): sorry about that — can you paste the request payload (no API key) and the exact error body?

JLee (customer): payload is small, here's redacted: ```json
{
  \"input\": [[\"first text\"], [\"second text\"]],
  \"model\": \"text-embed-001\"
}
```
error: `400 Bad Request: invalid input shape`

Sam (ENG): thanks — that payload is the issue. The embeddings endpoint expects `input` to be a list of strings (batch) or a single string. You're sending a nested array (array of arrays) so it becomes 3D when serialized.

JLee (customer): ohhh, we were trying to be clever because some entries are single vs list in our pipeline. we thought wrapping always in [] was safe. any quick fix?

Maria (Support): quick workaround: normalize before calling API. in JS something like: ```js
function normalizeInput(x){
  if(Array.isArray(x) && x.length === 1 && Array.isArray(x[0])) return x[0]; // unwrap double-wrap
  if(!Array.isArray(x)) return [String(x)];
  return x.map(String);
}
```
call with `input: normalizeInput(yourVariable)`

Ava (SRE): also note the retries — we saw a small billing spike from repeated 400 retries because client retried immediately. if you fix shape and backoff, that will stop unnecessary calls.

JLee (customer): got it. does the API return a helpful error message? it's pretty terse `invalid input shape` — could we get more detail like expected dims or example?

Sam (ENG): good feedback — backend currently validates and returns that generic message. we'll add a more specific error like `invalid input shape: expected [string] or [string,...], got nested arrays` and a doc snippet. I'll file a ticket.

Maria (Support): for your immediate debugging, check two common mistakes: 1) double-wrapped arrays like you had, 2) sending the JSON as a string accidentally (e.g., `input: JSON.stringify([...])`) — that will produce a single long string tokenized differently.

JLee (customer): aha — we also had code that did `payload.input = JSON.stringify(batch)` when logging, and then accidentally reused it. classic.

Sam (ENG): another edge case: some clients pass `input: { items: [...] }` or `inputs: [...]` (typo). server expects top-level `input`. we added validations for common typos in the SDK but not the raw API.

JLee (customer): when we corrected to `input: ["first text", "second text"]` it works. thanks. are there recommended sanity checks we can add to avoid regressions?

Maria (Support): yes — simple schema guard before send: ```js
if(!Array.isArray(payload.input)) payload.input = [payload.input];
if(!payload.input.every(it => typeof it === 'string')) throw new Error('bad input type');
```
Also set client-side metrics to count 400s for embeddings to alert on regressions.

Ava (SRE): we'll also add a temporary monitoring alert on elevated 4xx rates for /v1/embeddings from your org key while you roll out the fix — pinged infra (DeployBot).

DeployBot: Created ticket INFRA-5982 to add an alert for embedding 4xx spike for org jlee-inc.

Sam (ENG): followups from our side: 1) SDKs — add explicit shape validation and better error passthrough, 2) server — clearer error message for nested arrays, 3) docs — put example of single vs batch payloads and common JS pitfalls (JSON.stringify reuse). I'll put an ETA in the ticket.

JLee (customer): appreciate it. one more weirdness — we store vectors downstream in Pinecone and saw dimension mismatch errors after we fixed shape. any idea?

Sam (ENG): dimension mismatch usually means your downstream expected a fixed vector length (e.g., 1536) and got `null` or an object because earlier requests had failed or returned HTML. Confirm the successful response body contains `data[0].embedding.length === 1536` (or model-specific dim). sample success: ```json
{
  \"data\": [ { \"embedding\": [0.001, -0.002, ...], \"index\": 0 } ],
  \"model\": \"text-embed-001\"
}
```
If you see `embedding: null` or missing, don't write to DB. add a guard.

JLee (customer): good call — we were writing whatever came back without checking shape. fixed.

Maria (Support): summary and next steps: - customer fixed client double-wrapping and JSON reuse - customer added guards to avoid writing bad vectors - Support/ENG will improve error text + SDK validation + docs example - SRE added temporary alert for 4xx spike

JLee (customer): thanks everyone. saved us a morning. will reopen if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:

Sam (ENG): thanks — leaving this thread open until we ship the SDK/docs change. I’ll update INFRA-5982 and create a new ENG ticket for the server error message and SDK validation (ENG-embed-shape-fix).

Maria (Support): marking as escalated -> eng. closing after confirm deploy.

Ava (SRE): noted.
